findings.message: Charging semantics widened in step.ts pass 4 (lines 476-484): every targeted request whose type is in the one sighting message is answered 'sighting', so two requests with different ids for the same type in one step both get 'sighting' and both are charged 25 gold for a single sighting entry. This applies before minute 28 (the second used to be 'capped') and after it (the 'lift the sighting cap from the carrier reveal on' test still expects ['sighting','sighting'], but the two requests now share one message and one entry). Also, a request whose type a free trigger in the same step already asks for is charged for a sighting the player would have got for free. The worker disclosed this in open assumptions and docs/intel.md, and it follows the literal task wording. Still, it conflicts with the intel-core intent that gold is charged only for something delivered. The caller (objectives-endgame) should decide whether to answer a second same-type request (or one covered by a free trigger) as not charged.
findings.requirement: answer each targeted request in it `sighting`

findings.message: A pending type joins the accumulator only on a step that crosses a snapshot boundary (step.ts:406-409 and 480). With the default rules this is harmless: between boundaries a pending type is either capped or has no snapshot data. But validateIntelRules does not require carrierRevealTicks to be a multiple of carrierIntervalTicks. With a misaligned reveal, a type capped before minute 28 stays pending past the reveal, and a new loss in that gap goes out in its own uncapped message, so the two reach the player in separate messages up to one interval apart. Either require the alignment in the validator or merge the pending set into the accumulator whenever the player is uncapped.
findings.requirement: It starts with the player's pending set if a boundary was crossed.

findings.message: No test checks that a sighting message's type order and sector choice are independent of the order in which triggers joined the accumulator. In every multi-type scripted case in packages/simulation/src/intel/intel.test.ts (lines 447-605: the pending sun+moon pair, pending sun/moon/tide, two losses, a sun loss plus a storm replacement, a sun loss plus a storm request, a batched sun+moon, and a pending sun plus a moon loss on the boundary tick), triggers join in an order that already matches type order (sun, moon, tide, storm). Each of those types also has exactly one sector option, so no sector draw is ever contested. The property Checker (property.test.ts:425-455) never checks the order of the sightings or the sector choice against trigger order. Two regressions would therefore pass the whole suite: dropping the `.sort(byTypeOrder)` at step.ts:468 (the message would then follow Map insertion order), or drawing each sector when its trigger is added. A missing test would need triggers that arrive out of type order, for example a moon loss plus a sun replacement, or a pending storm plus a sun loss on a boundary, with at least two sectors per type. It would then compare against the same step with the triggers in the opposite order.
findings.requirement: The message's type order and sector choice must not depend on the order in which triggers were added.

findings.message: The property Checker records each sighting's reason without checking it. property.test.ts:438 only does EXERCISED.add(`sighting:${sighting.reason}`), and CarrierSighting.reason is typed IntelLeadReason, which includes "start" (state.ts:295). So the eight seeded runs, which include late joiners and carried-only worlds, would still pass if a start produced a carrier sighting. Only two scripted worlds prove that a start never sights (intel.test.ts:150-169 and 199-201). The checker should reject any sighting whose reason is not fresh, targeted or replacement.
findings.requirement: A start never produces a carrier sighting, as `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` specifies (sightings only on a fresh loss, a targeted rumor, or a journal replacement).
